- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -1.00) in recent history, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to avoid undershooting.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; add 0.5–1.5% to early forecast values.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 3–5 day horizon.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias toward lower prices after 10+ consecutive days of high values; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment if recent 10-day average is above 65.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after day 10, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for days 11–20.
